title: UA vs UARK: tuition, size, location
summary: University of Alabama in Huntsville (UA) versus University of Arkansas at Little Rock (UARK). Also searched as UARK vs UA. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: The University of Arkansas at Little Rock (UARK) and the University of Alabama in Huntsville (UA) are both public institutions, but they differ in several key aspects. UARK, located in Little Rock, has an undergraduate enrollment of 4,949 students, whereas UA in Huntsville enrolls 6,591 undergraduates. Tuition for in-state students at UARK is $9,748, which is lower compared to UA's in-state tuition of $12,132. These differences reflect variations in size, location, and cost between the two universities.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing the cost of attendance between the University of Arkansas at Little Rock (UARK) and the University of Alabama in Huntsville (UA), UARK offers lower tuition rates for both in-state and out-of-state students. In-state tuition at UARK is $9,748, while UA charges $12,132 for in-state students. For out-of-state students, UARK's tuition is $22,158, compared to UA's $26,408. Regarding student debt, the median amount owed by completers at UARK is $22,000, slightly higher than UA's median debt of $20,705. These figures highlight differences in affordability and financial outcomes for students attending these two public universities.

sections.heading: Learning model and campus
paragraphs: The University of Arkansas at Little Rock (UARK) and the University of Alabama in Huntsville (UA) both offer primarily on-campus learning experiences in their respective cities. UARK is situated in Little Rock, Arkansas, and serves an undergraduate population of 4,949 students. In contrast, UA is located in Huntsville, Alabama, with a larger undergraduate enrollment of 6,591 students. Both institutions provide traditional campus environments that support in-person instruction and student engagement.
